title: Dual-valve, air-sealed siphon-jet toilet with rim-wash optimization

locations.name: California (testing standards)
locations.basis: Transcript cites California as the context for the strict water-restriction standard (1.28 gpf) used in tests.

summary: This Old House explores the development of a low-consumption toilet at an engineering design facility. The episode traces the workflow from computer-driven hydraulics simulations to rapid prototyping and a battery of bench tests designed to preserve flushing performance under tighter water use. A core innovation demonstrated is a dual-flush system that separates the rim-wash function from the siphon-jet bowl flush and is sealed to air to avoid an air-gap that would sap flush power. The tests cover drain-line carry (4-inch pipe, pitch, and length), low-water flush (1.28 gal per flush), bulk waste removal (miso paste), and mixed-media flush performance, with attention to rim cleanliness and the elimination of dirt-trapping undercuts. The video also includes a cutaway explanation of toilet internals (trap seal, siphon jet, flush valves) and notes homeowner complaints about rim-wash under low-flow conditions.

sections.title: Facility purpose and water-efficiency goals
sections.description: Introduces the engineering facility’s mission to re-engineer plumbing products for higher efficiency while maintaining bulk waste removal, bowl cleaning, and drain-line performance. Sets the context that toilets are a major home water consumer and must meet growing efficiency demands.

sections.title: Computer simulations of hydraulics and performance goals
sections.description: Shows computer simulations used to measure water velocity, flow power, and consumption, with the aim of achieving an optimum hydraulic performance before physical prototyping.

sections.title: Planning for rapid prototyping and integration of form and function
sections.description: Outlines the transition from virtual models to physical prototypes and emphasizes planning to test performance before finalizing the toilet’s look.

sections.title: Design-to-test alignment with industry standards
sections.description: Discusses designing the toilet to meet industry standards while also developing a visually appealing product.

sections.title: Drain line carry test setup and specifications
sections.description: Details the drain-line carry test using a 4-inch drain line with a typical 1/4 inch per foot pitch, referencing the toughest water-restriction standards (California) to validate performance.

sections.title: Poly-ball flush test and preliminary results
sections.description: Describes flushing 103? (poly balls) to simulate waste and verify the system clears the line to around 40+ feet with a 1.28 gallons-per-flush standard.

sections.title: Mixed-media flush test (bulk removal capability)
sections.description: Introduces a mixed-media test (2500 items with varied buoyancies) to confirm the toilet can flush out nearly all material from the bowl under low-water conditions.

sections.title: Bulk-waste removal test with miso paste
sections.description: Demonstrates testing with miso paste in a sleeve, progressively challenging the system to remove bulk waste beyond minimum requirements (up to 12 links).

sections.title: Rim-wash concerns and internal cutaway explanation
sections.description: Addresses homeowner complaints about rim-wash effectiveness and presents a cutaway showing how water and waste move through the trap seal and rim during flush.

sections.title: Air-gap issue and siphon-jet power preservation
sections.description: Explains how an air gap between bowl and tank can reduce flush velocity, and why solving this is critical to maintaining power in low-flow toilets.

sections.title: Dual-valve approach: rim area vs siphon-jet area
sections.description: Shows the separation of the rim-area flush valve from the bowl siphon-jet valve, with the siphon-jet valve sealed to air to prevent air ingress.

sections.title: Water-split optimization for flush power
sections.description: Describes the targeted water split: about 30% to fire the siphon trap and 70% for rim wash to keep the bowl clean.

sections.title: Final flush demonstration and design takeaways
sections.description: Demonstrates a flush using 1.28 gallons, showing effective removal and highlighting design changes like eliminating undercuts and creating a strong cleaning jet.
